stories.title: U.S. and Iran trade strikes. How will this affect deal to end war?
stories.summary: Do new strikes affect a potential deal to end the war with Iran? NPR's Scott Detrow breaks it down with NPR International Correspondent Aya Batrawy and NPR Pentagon Correspondent Tom Bowman.

stories.title: Knicks superfan Spike Lee says his team will definitely win the Championship
stories.summary: NPR's Juana Summers speaks with filmmaker Spike Lee about his excitement that his favorite basketball team, the New York Knicks, making it to the NBA finals.

stories.title: Black homeowners in St. Louis are still awaiting aid a year after destructive tornado
stories.summary: Decades of disinvestment in a predominantly Black St. Louis neighborhood left the community especially vulnerable to last year's devastating tornadoes. Now, some worry homeownership rates will drop.

stories.title: FBI trains local and state police on how to stop growing threat of drones
stories.summary: The upcoming FIFA World Cup is prompting the FBI to ramp up training for law enforcement on how to stop a growing threat: malicious drones in U.S. skies.

stories.title: Remembering Clarence B. Jones, MLK adviser who helped write 'I Have a Dream' speech
stories.summary: Clarence B. Jones, a lawyer and adviser to the Rev. Martin Luther King Jr., died last week. Jones helped King write his famous "I Have a Dream" speech. He was 95.

stories.title: NAACP calls for sports boycott in states where voting rights are threatened
stories.summary: NPR's Juana Summers talks with NAACP President and CEO Derrick Johnson about his organization's Out of Bounds campaign that draws a connection between Black student athletes and voting rights.
